body.x: Toshiba (www.toshiba.com), a Fortune Global 500 electronics company, unveiled "Toshiba Glass," a lifelike robot, and other products at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.Toshiba Glass is a B2B solution that enables quick retrieval of manuals and other information while doing maintenance and logistics work away from a computer.It is a small, light projection module which achieved maximum portability with foldable glass and detachable projection module.It can be used for maintenance and construction work site for tunnels, power plants, communication hubs, and many other sites where retrieval of manual is necessary but the access to a computer is unavailable. The use for this solution can be boundless, to sectors such as medical and healthcare, warehouse and logistics, law enforcement, fire authorities, security, museum, theaters, amusement parks, stadiums, retail stores and more.

A lifelike robot "ChihiraAico" can be programmed to execute a variety of activities, thus being able to handle tasks for many occupations. A virtual fitting system "Coordinate Plus" uses body scanning technology to enable shoppers to try on clothing remotely via a tablet or mobile device.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot.
